n46016b991aa.s: After abolishing the Dual Government in 1772, Warren Hastings shifted the treasury from Murshidabad to:
n46016b991aa.x: Hastings moved the treasury from Murshidabad to Calcutta after ending the Dual Government in 1772.

n0cc8028b75c.s: Before the Bengal Famine of 1770, the high land revenue was collected in ____, forcing peasants to sell grain.
n0cc8028b75c.x: High land revenue demanded in cash forced peasants to sell grain, one of the causes of the 1770 famine.

n7af215a5baa.s: Anandamath (1882), which contains the song Vande Mataram, was written by:
n7af215a5baa.x: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay published Anandamath in 1882; it contains Vande Mataram.

n81a7634b263.s: R.P. Dutt placed the drain of Bengal's surplus revenue after 1765 in the mercantilist phase, which he dated:
n81a7634b263.x: R.P. Dutt dated the mercantilist phase 1757-1813, when Bengal's surplus revenue bought Indian goods for export.

n31b2092efb1.s: Under the Dual Government, the East India Company collected revenue through:
o: Indian deputies acting on its behalf
Direct collection by British district collectors
Village panchayats appointed by the Nawab
n31b2092efb1.x: The Company did not collect revenue itself at first; it worked through Indian deputies.

n38756dc60cf.s: Who was the last Governor of Bengal (1772-73) and the first Governor-General of Bengal (1773)?
n38756dc60cf.x: Warren Hastings was the last Governor of Bengal (1772-73) and became the first Governor-General of Bengal in 1773.

n92fa16fee19.s: During the Bengal Famine of 1770, the Company:
o: gave little or no relief and kept collecting revenue
stopped all exports and remitted land revenue permanently
handed famine administration to the Nawab without conditions
provided extensive relief and suspended revenue collection
n92fa16fee19.x: The Company offered little or no relief and continued collecting revenue during the famine.

n0d0e411c2a5.s: Who among the following was a leader of the Sanyasi-Fakir Revolt?
n0d0e411c2a5.x: Majnum Shah (with Bhawani Pathak and Devi Chaudhurani) led the Sanyasi-Fakir Revolt; Shah Alam II was not a leader of it.

n85888f9d3c7.s: After the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War, who was placed on the restored Wodeyar throne of Mysore as a boy ruler?
n85888f9d3c7.x: After the Fourth War the Wodeyar dynasty was restored with the boy ruler Krishnaraja Wodeyar III, under a Subsidiary Alliance. (No dated events for a sequence question, so written as a one-liner.)

na063bf469f0.s: The Jacobin Club at Seringapatam, of which 'Citizen Tipu' became a member, was established in:
na063bf469f0.x: The Jacobin Club was set up at Seringapatam in 1797; Tipu joined it, called himself 'Citizen Tipu' and planted a Tree of Liberty.

n2158f054e5e.s: The Treaty of Mangalore (1784) was concluded between the British and:
n2158f054e5e.x: The Treaty of Mangalore (1784) was made with Tipu Sultan; the Treaty of Madras (1769) was made with Haidar Ali.

n58072dd0729.s: Under the Treaty of Seringapatam (1792), Malabar, Coorg (as protectorate), Dindigul and the Bara Mahal went to:
n58072dd0729.x: The British took Malabar, Coorg, Dindigul and the Bara Mahal; the Nizam got the Krishna-Pennar area and the Marathas the Tungabhadra area.

nd961b833d38.s: In the early Anglo-Mysore Wars, Thomas Munro served under Hector Munro and:
nd961b833d38.x: Hector Munro and Sir Eyre Coote were British commanders in the early wars, and Thomas Munro served under both.

ncf8eef50c25.s: Haidar Ali became Faujdar of Dindigul in 1755 under the Mysore minister:
ncf8eef50c25.x: Haidar Ali rose under the Wodeyars and became Faujdar of Dindigul in 1755 under the minister Nanjaraja.

nindian-history-17-41.s: At the start of the Second Anglo-Mysore War (1780-84), Haidar Ali was allied with:
o: the Nawab of Arcot and the Marathas
the Nizam and the Nawab of Arcot
nindian-history-17-41.x: The Second Anglo-Mysore War began with Haidar Ali allied to the Nizam and the Marathas.

nindian-history-17-39.s: The First Anglo-Mysore War, led on the Mysore side by Haidar Ali, ended in 1769 with the Treaty of:
nindian-history-17-39.x: Haidar Ali came out on top near Madras and the war ended with the Treaty of Madras (1769).

nindian-history-17-42.s: At the Battle of Porto Novo (July 1781), Haidar Ali was defeated by:
nindian-history-17-42.x: Sir Eyre Coote led the British to victory over Haidar Ali at Porto Novo in the Second Anglo-Mysore War.

nindian-history-19-19.s: Which battle reversed the British defeat at Pollilur (1780)?
nindian-history-19-19.x: Coote's defeat of Haidar Ali at Porto Novo (1781) reversed the British disaster at Pollilur (1780).

n8e7e528ec87.s:
Assertion (A): By 1801 the whole Andhra region had come under the Company.
Reason (R): Nellore and Chittoor were annexed from the Carnatic Nawab in 1801.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n8e7e528ec87.x: The 1801 acquisition of Nellore and Chittoor completed Company control over the Andhra region, so R explains A.

n983bc79beac.s: Kandregula Jogipantulu proposed ₹15 lakh a year for the Circar lease, but the final 1766 treaty fixed it at:
n983bc79beac.x: Jogipantulu proposed ₹15 lakh using the Gollapudi pay mutiny, but the 1766 treaty fixed ₹9 lakh a year.

nindian-history-91-19.s: The Ring Fence Policy aimed at:
o: a strong monarchy and suppression of rebellion
creating buffer states to protect Company territories
annexation of states without a natural male heir
an independent foreign policy avoiding power blocs
nindian-history-91-19.x: The Ring Fence Policy sought buffer states to protect Company territories.

n4971cb9fdd7.s: Under the Subsidiary Alliance, if a ruler failed to pay for the subsidiary force, the result was:
o: an increase in the subsidy rate
transfer of the force to a neighbouring state
n4971cb9fdd7.x: The ruler paid in cash or by ceding territory; failure to pay led to territorial cession, not withdrawal of the force.

n3d0351cdc9a.s: Who led the attack on the Hyderabad Residency on 17 July 1857 to free Chida Khan?
n3d0351cdc9a.x: Turrebaz Khan attacked the Residency on 17 July 1857 to free Chida Khan; Davidson repulsed the attack.

n100de4c3e5e.s: The Nizam's 'Ceded Districts' arose from which consequence of the Subsidiary Alliance?
o: Territorial cession when subsidies were unpaid
Conquest in the Fourth Mysore War
Annexation under the Doctrine of Lapse
n100de4c3e5e.x: The Subsidiary Alliance led to territorial cessions when subsidies were unpaid, such as the Nizam's Ceded Districts.

n8df2d73a433.s: Under the Subsidiary Alliance, which of the following was a function of the British Resident at Hyderabad?
o: Exercising hereditary succession to the Nizam's throne
Presiding over the Madras Board of Revenue
n8df2d73a433.x: The Resident controlled the Nizam's foreign relations and supervised the subsidiary force; he had no hereditary right to the throne.

nd6cec858b4a.s: Awadh was annexed in 1856 on the ground of:
nd6cec858b4a.x: Awadh was annexed in 1856 on the ground of maladministration (Punjab, by contrast, was annexed by conquest).

neafaaf5397f.s: Besides succession disputes and misgovernment, the British justified intervening in princely states' internal affairs by the need to:
neafaaf5397f.x: The British claimed intervention to fulfil their international commitments, and also intervened in succession disputes and misgovernment.

n24550f643a0.s: Which was the first state to accept the Subsidiary Alliance, in 1798?
n24550f643a0.x: Hyderabad was the first state (1798); Tipu refused it, and Holkar signed only in 1818 as the last Maratha power.

nindian-history-91-12.s: Which policy provided for the annexation of states without a natural male heir?
nindian-history-91-12.x: The Doctrine of Lapse annexed states without a natural male heir.

nindian-history-91-18.s: The Doctrine of Lapse is associated with:
nindian-history-91-18.x: The Doctrine of Lapse belongs to Dalhousie, not Warren Hastings.

nf67210b7260.s: In which year did Nizam Ali agree to lease the Northern Circars to the British?
nf67210b7260.x: Nizam Ali leased the Circars in 1766, after Salabat Jung's grant (1759) and before the Treaty of Masulipatnam (1768) and the Guntur handover (1788).

nap-history-10-4.s: Which Andhra officer helped Sir Arthur Cotton build the Godavari barrage?
nap-history-10-4.x: Veneti (Veenam) Veeranna helped Cotton build the Godavari barrage; G.N. Taylor opened Anglo-vernacular schools at Rajahmundry.

n30a7ae4d76e.s: Which of the following are present-day silk hubs of Rayalaseema?
n30a7ae4d76e.x: Dharmavaram and Madanapalle are present-day silk hubs; sericulture was promoted by the British in the Ceded Districts in the late 19th-early 20th centuries.

ne4f6e01768f.s: Vizianagaram, Bobbili and Pithapuram were estates under the ____ system.
ne4f6e01768f.x: Vizianagaram, Bobbili and Pithapuram were Zamindari estates; Ryotwari dealt directly with the ryot.

nbfde8881932.s: The Nizam ceded the 'Ceded Districts' to the British in:
nbfde8881932.x: The Nizam ceded them in 1800 because he could not pay the Subsidiary Alliance subsidy in cash.

n0bcb4db64e6.s: Under Company revenue administration, the officer at the taluk level was the:
n0bcb4db64e6.x: The Board of Revenue was at state level, the Collector at district, the Tahsildar at taluk and the Karanam and Munsab at village level.

n9bd44af3ade.s: The Battle of Padmanabham was fought in:
n9bd44af3ade.x: The Battle of Padmanabham was fought in 1794.

n72801583fd4.s: Thomas Munro was President of the Judicial Commission constituted in:
n72801583fd4.x: Munro presided over the Judicial Commission of 1814; its report was submitted in April 1816 and largely accepted.

o: inland transit and customs duties on goods
a tax on looms and occupations
n42f83d81a0a.x: Sayer was the inland transit and customs duty; Abkari was excise on liquor and Moturpha a tax on looms and trades.

n0fd23889ddc.s: The Indian Penal Code was enacted in:
n0fd23889ddc.x: The IPC dates to 1860; the CPC to 1859 and the CrPC to 1861.

n2a6b5537f74.s: A Supreme Court plea seeking a separate revenue judicial service cadre, since revenue officers lack legal training to decide land-title disputes, invoked:
n2a6b5537f74.x: The plea invoked Article 14; the Supreme Court issued notice on it.

n0a445c739c1.s: Which of the following came under Company rule last?
n0a445c739c1.x: The Circars came in 1766, Guntur in 1788, the Ceded Districts in 1800 and Nellore-Chittoor last, in 1801.

n79b85f088ce.s: Zamindari was abolished in the Madras Presidency in:
n79b85f088ce.x: Zamindari in Madras was abolished in 1948, after Guntur (1788), Padmanabham (1794) and the extension of Ryotwari (1820).

n6f6605cceb9.s: The Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam was concluded in:
n6f6605cceb9.x: The Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam came in 1798, after the Treaty of Masulipatnam (1768), the Guntur handover (1788) and Padmanabham (1794).

n9c916e396a9.s: An important effect of the Zamindari system in the Northern Circars was:
o: uniform assessment limited to one-fourth of the produce
transfer of all land rights to village headmen
absentee landlordism and impoverishment of tenants
n9c916e396a9.x: The Zamindari system encouraged absentee landlordism and impoverished tenants.

n3bc853063e1.s: Which of the following was one of the five traditional Circars of the Northern Circars?
n3bc853063e1.x: The five Circars were Chicacole, Rajahmundry, Ellore, Mustafanagar and Guntur; Masulipatnam was a Company station, not a Circar.

nb5dcd88dfd3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Dowleswaram anicut?
o: Arthur Cotton reported to the Board of Revenue on it in 1844.
Work on it began in 1847 and its main work was completed in April 1852.
Its Indian assistant Veenam Veeranna was made Rao Bahadur and Assistant Engineer.
nb5dcd88dfd3.x: Cotton reported in 1844, but the anicut was sanctioned only in late 1846.

n5c79a6373cf.s: The Buckingham Canal, a salt-water navigation canal along the coast through Pulicat Lake, is part of:
n5c79a6373cf.x: The Buckingham Canal is part of NW-4 (Kakinada-Puducherry), not NW-5.

nae13c7e91c8.s: The First Anglo-Sikh War was fought when the Governor-General was:
nae13c7e91c8.x: The First Anglo-Sikh War belonged to Hardinge; Dalhousie fought the Second.

n2a30b0b9ebb.s: Discontent among many sepoys before the Revolt of 1857 was linked to the annexation of:
n2a30b0b9ebb.x: The annexation of Awadh fed discontent among many Awadh sepoys, one of the causes of resentment before 1857.

nd88f62819fd.s: Mysore's control over which Malabar spices was a factor in the British conflicts with Mysore?
nd88f62819fd.x: The British were concerned about Mysore's control of Malabar pepper and cardamom, its threat to Madras and its French ties.

nce09a810bd0.s: The Treaty of Madras (1769), which ended the First Anglo-Mysore War, provided for:
o: cession of half of Mysore's territory
mutual restitution of conquests and a defensive alliance
nce09a810bd0.x: The Treaty of Madras gave mutual restitution of conquests and a defensive alliance.

nd1f0508e5b1.s: Under British paramountcy, Indian states generally retained:
o: the right to make war on neighbours
nd1f0508e5b1.x: Indian states kept their internal administration but had no independent international life.

n923f57313b9.s: The Treaty of Deogaon (1803) was signed by the British with:
n923f57313b9.x: Deogaon was with the Bhonsle of Nagpur; Bassein with the Peshwa, Surji-Arjangaon with Scindia and Rajpurghat with Holkar.

nindian-history-17-49.s: Who led the Sikhs at the Battle of Chillianwala?
nindian-history-17-49.x: Sher Singh Attariwala led the Sikhs and Lord Gough the British; the battle was undecided.

nindian-history-81-16.s: The Treaty of Salbai made peace between the British and the:
nindian-history-81-16.x: The Treaty of Salbai brought British-Maratha peace.

nf3174b31410.x: By 1856 British India stretched from the Hindukush to Burma, giving geographical unity and a basis for common resistance.

n3e5603c618b.s: The Ceded Districts, given up by the Nizam in 1800, came to be called:
n3e5603c618b.x: Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary, ceded in 1800, were called the Ceded Districts or Dattamandalalu.

nd8e2c7421d8.s: Coorg was annexed in 1834 on the plea of misgovernance by:
nd8e2c7421d8.x: Bentinck took Coorg in 1834 citing misgovernance, along with Central Cachar.

nindian-history-106-2.s: The policy of non-intervention is associated with:
nindian-history-106-2.x: Sir John Shore followed non-intervention; Hastings the Ring Fence, Cornwallis the Permanent Settlement, Wellesley the Subsidiary Alliance.

nindian-history-106-7.s: The First Anglo-Burmese War took place under:
nindian-history-106-7.x: The First Anglo-Burmese War came under Amherst; Auckland had the First Afghan War and Ellenborough annexed Sindh.

n77dbb8bc18b.s: Who was the Governor-General during the Second Anglo-Mysore War (1780-84)?
n77dbb8bc18b.x: Warren Hastings was Governor-General during the Second war; Cornwallis fought the Third.

ne1b2b7b14d5.s: The Third Anglo-Maratha War, in which the Peshwa attacked the Poona Residency, occurred under:
ne1b2b7b14d5.x: The Third Anglo-Maratha War came during Lord Hastings' tenure; afterwards the office of Peshwa was abolished.

nf84a965c19a.s: Who commanded the British forces at Assaye?
nf84a965c19a.x: Arthur Wellesley commanded at Assaye; Lord Lake at Delhi and Laswari; Gough at Mudki and Chillianwala.

nfde2916ba94.s: Tipu Sultan is said to have planted a 'Tree of Liberty' at:
nfde2916ba94.x: The Tree of Liberty was planted at Srirangapatnam, his capital; Dindigul is where Haidar Ali set up an arsenal in 1755.

nindian-history-81-4.s: The Treaty of Salbai was signed in:
nindian-history-81-4.x: Salbai was 1782; Madras 1769, Allahabad 1765 and Bassein 1802.

nb34db7ba5bc.s: After the First Anglo-Sikh War, Kashmir was transferred to Gulab Singh under the Treaty of:
nb34db7ba5bc.x: Kashmir went to Gulab Singh under a separate Treaty of Amritsar; Bhairowal also followed the First Anglo-Sikh War.

nb85a63a8bcc.s: Baji Rao II, whose adopted son Nana Sahib was denied the Peshwa pension, died in:
nb85a63a8bcc.x: Baji Rao II died in 1851, after which Nana Sahib's pension was stopped.

nindian-history-81-7.s: The Treaty of Yandabo ended the:
nindian-history-81-7.x: Yandabo (1826) ended the First Anglo-Burmese War; Sugauli (1815) ended the Anglo-Nepal War.

nindian-history-106-1.s: Warren Hastings served as Governor-General of Bengal during:
nindian-history-106-1.x: Warren Hastings, the first Governor-General of Bengal, held the post from 1774 to 1785.

nindian-history-106-4.s: Lord Wellesley, who introduced the Subsidiary Alliance, served as Governor-General during:
nindian-history-106-4.x: Wellesley ruled from 1798 to 1805, introduced the Subsidiary Alliance and fought the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.

nindian-history-81-14.s: The Treaty of Lahore (1846) followed which war?
nindian-history-81-14.x: The Treaty of Lahore (1846) followed the First Anglo-Sikh War and extended British control in Punjab.

n92638334fbe.s: Which of the following series of wars began first?
n92638334fbe.x: The Anglo-Mysore Wars began in 1767, before the Anglo-Maratha (1775) and Anglo-Sikh (1845) Wars.

n17f81cd063c.s: The press in India was liberated under:
n17f81cd063c.x: Metcalfe liberated the press; Bentinck suppressed Thuggee, Dalhousie set up the PWD and Hastings had the Code of Gentoo Laws compiled.

n52ad6de3f38.s: The impeachment trial of Warren Hastings (1788-1795) ended in his:
n52ad6de3f38.x: Burke and the Whigs impeached Hastings in 1787; the trial ran 1788-1795 and ended in acquittal.

nindian-history-97-10.s: The Regulating Act and the Ring Fence policy are associated with:
nindian-history-97-10.x: Warren Hastings is linked with the Regulating Act and Ring Fence policy; Clive with Plassey, Cornwallis with the Permanent Settlement, Wellesley with the Subsidiary Alliance.

n2f9b2147fc3.s: Who became the first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act of 1833?
n2f9b2147fc3.x: Bentinck became the first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act of 1833; Canning was the first Viceroy.

n49da67cda2c.s: The post of District Judge was created by:
n49da67cda2c.x: Cornwallis created the post of District Judge; his Code of 1793 separated revenue from justice.

n8924a607515.s: The Anti-Slavery Act of 1843 was passed under:
n8924a607515.x: The 1843 Anti-Slavery Act was Ellenborough's; Hardinge I is linked to the Anti-Human-Sacrifice Act of 1845.

n11dfcc18d8c.s: The College of Fort William (1800) was founded by:
n11dfcc18d8c.x: The College of Fort William (1800) was Wellesley's, not Warren Hastings'.

n7c483c33a11.s: The first universities in India were established in 1857 during the tenure of:
n7c483c33a11.x: The first universities came in 1857 under Canning, not Bentinck.

n5cf739ebcca.x: Sati was abolished under Bentinck in 1829 (after Wellesley's infanticide measure of 1802 and before Ellenborough's 1843 slavery abolition).

nindian-history-97-21.s: Albuquerque captured Goa for the Portuguese in:
nindian-history-97-21.x: Albuquerque captured Goa in 1510; Almeida's Blue Water Policy was an earlier, separate strategy.

n354b30af5fe.s: Which of the following was among the impeachment charges against Warren Hastings?
o: Plunder of the Begums of Awadh
Introduction of the Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam
Application of the Doctrine of Lapse
n354b30af5fe.x: The charges included the Rohilla War, Chait Singh, the plunder of the Begums of Awadh and the judicial murder of Nand Kumar.

nfa6ccbadc7b.s: In 1831 William Bentinck concluded a treaty of perpetual friendship with:
nfa6ccbadc7b.x: Bentinck concluded a treaty of perpetual friendship with Ranjit Singh in 1831.

nindian-history-125-9.s: The capital was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi during the viceroyalty of:
nindian-history-125-9.x: Hardinge II is linked with the shift of capital and the Delhi Durbar of 1911.

nindian-history-125-17.s: Chauri Chaura and the Swaraj Party belong to the viceroyalty of:
nindian-history-125-17.x: Reading is linked with Chauri Chaura and the Swaraj Party; Irwin with the Simon Commission and Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

n6ea5f8ccbe7.s: The portfolio system was introduced during the tenure of:
n6ea5f8ccbe7.x: Canning's tenure saw the Indian Councils Act 1861, the portfolio system, the first universities and the IPC.

nb34ebe3d5ac.s: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 during the viceroyalty of:
nb34ebe3d5ac.x: The INC was founded under Dufferin; the Durand Commission came under Lansdowne and the Chapekar killings under Elgin II.

n32a06fb52f1.s: The Indian Independence Act, which abolished the offices of Viceroy and Secretary of State, was passed on:
n32a06fb52f1.x: The Indian Independence Act of 18 July 1947 abolished the offices of Viceroy and Secretary of State.

n9336414b3c7.s: Queen Victoria was proclaimed Empress of India at the 1877 Delhi Durbar under:

nab91790f524.s: The Archaeological Survey of India was set up in 1861 under:
nab91790f524.x: The ASI was set up in 1861 under Canning, with Cunningham as founder; Curzon later revived it.

n982a05063d7.s: The Cabinet Mission of 1946 consisted of Cripps, A.V. Alexander and:
n982a05063d7.x: The Cabinet Mission members were Cripps, A.V. Alexander and Pethick-Lawrence.

nindian-history-25-16.s: Who was the first Archaeological Surveyor of India?
nindian-history-25-16.x: Alexander Cunningham was the first Archaeological Surveyor; John Marshall later became Director-General.

nindian-history-106-12.s: The Vernacular Press Act (1878) was repealed in 1882 by:
nindian-history-106-12.x: Lytton passed the Vernacular Press Act in 1878 and Ripon repealed it in 1882.

n99eb020d0e3.x: Raleigh dealt with universities; Hunter with education, Durand with the Afghan boundary and Lyall with famine.

ne9c90245f51.s: The annulment of the Partition of Bengal and the transfer of the capital to Delhi were announced at the Delhi Durbar on:
ne9c90245f51.x: Both, with the creation of Bihar and Orissa, were announced on 12 December 1911.

nff32f4fad91.s: Lord Lytton's Royal Titles Act was passed in:
nff32f4fad91.x: The Royal Titles Act came in 1876, after Mayo's 1870 resolution and before Ripon's 1881 Factory Act.

nb1e0c039671.s: Which Viceroy came immediately after Lord Minto II?
nb1e0c039671.x: The order is Curzon, Minto II, Hardinge II, Chelmsford and Reading.

nccc0672f637.s: The August Offer was made in:
nccc0672f637.x: The August Offer was in 1940, between the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931) and the Wavell Plan (1945).

nindian-history-125-3.s: The policy of 'Masterly Inactivity' towards Afghanistan is associated with:
nindian-history-125-3.x: Masterly Inactivity was Lord Lawrence's (1864-69) policy of non-interference in Afghanistan.

n3e16fe38c9a.s: Which Act directed the Supreme Court at Calcutta to respect the personal laws of Hindus and Muslims?
n3e16fe38c9a.x: The Amending Act of 1781 (Act of Settlement) required the Court to respect Hindu and Muslim personal laws and exempted official acts.

n0e44160bcf6.s: The Act of 1786 was passed to meet the condition of which Governor-General for accepting office?
n0e44160bcf6.x: The Act of 1786 met Cornwallis's condition, letting the GG override his Council and act as Commander-in-Chief.

nf3ae880af3f.s: The Select Committee appointed by Parliament in 1772 to inquire into Company affairs was headed by:
nf3ae880af3f.x: In 1772 Parliament appointed a Select Committee under Burgoyne along with a Secret Committee.

n4391584716e.s: Pitt's India Act was passed in:
n4391584716e.x: The order was Regulating Act 1773, Amending Act 1781, Pitt's India Act 1784 and Act of 1786.

nda842c3edfb.s: The overriding power given to the Governor-General by the Act of 1786 corrected which defect of the Regulating Act?
o: The absence of a Board of Control
The absence of a Supreme Court at Calcutta
The repeated outvoting of the Governor-General by his Council
nda842c3edfb.x: The Act of 1786 addressed the Governor-General, including Hastings, being repeatedly outvoted by his Council.

n2e2b2da8e1d.s: The 'Double Government' set up by Pitt's India Act (1784) was ended by the:
n2e2b2da8e1d.x: Pitt's India Act created the dual system, which lasted until the Government of India Act of 1858.

n5d64e573342.s: The Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774) consisted of one Chief Justice and:
n5d64e573342.x: It had one Chief Justice and three judges with civil and criminal jurisdiction.

n271cc3532a6.s: The first step by the British Parliament to control the East India Company was the:
n271cc3532a6.x: The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first parliamentary measure to control the Company and recognised its political and administrative functions.

n21a3dc03e72.s: Under the Regulating Act of 1773, the Governor-General:
o: could override his Council in special cases
had an unrestricted veto over his Council
could be outvoted by his Council
n21a3dc03e72.x: The Governor-General had no veto and could be outvoted by his Council; the override power came only with the Act of 1786.

n6c1e82a2360.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Charter Act of 1853?
o: The other two new legislative members were the Commander-in-Chief and the Law Member.
Six new legislative members were added.
The new members formed a separate Central Legislative Council.
Four members were appointed by Madras, Bombay, Bengal and Agra, the first local representation.
n6c1e82a2360.x: The two remaining members were not the Commander-in-Chief and the Law Member; they included the Chief Justice.

ne1d8a09c9c0.s: The Act of 1773 made the Governor of Bengal the:
ne1d8a09c9c0.x: The 1773 Act created the Governor-General of Bengal and subordinated Bombay and Madras.

n3cb40cde2b7.s: The Charter Act of 1813 provided an annual education grant of:
n3cb40cde2b7.x: The grant was Rs 1,00,000 (1 lakh) a year, the first step towards State responsibility for education; Rs 10 lakh is a misprint.

n88a33e6ad92.s: Under the Charter Act of 1833, laws made by the Governor-General-in-Council were called:
n88a33e6ad92.x: From 1833 laws were called Acts instead of Regulations, and legislative power for all British India went to the GG-in-Council.

n1a45786302c.s: The Macaulay Committee on the Indian Civil Service was constituted in:
n1a45786302c.x: The Macaulay Committee (1854) recommended competitive examinations in place of nomination and favoured graduates.

n64ea4edd269.s: The first Law Commission (1834), which drafted the Indian Penal Code, was chaired by:
n64ea4edd269.x: The first Law Commission was set up in 1834 under Macaulay and drafted the IPC.

nc8596183b79.s: The last Charter Act of the East India Company was the Charter Act of:
nc8596183b79.x: The Charter Act of 1853 was the last; the Government of India Act of 1858 then transferred authority to the Crown.

n059b196169a.s: Which Charter Act officially allowed Christian missionaries to enter India?
n059b196169a.x: Under Evangelical pressure (Wilberforce, Charles Grant), the Charter Act of 1813 allowed missionaries to enter and preach.

naf8ca318a1e.s:
Assertion (A): Under the Ryotwari settlement, revenue was fixed on the land rather than directly on the crop produced.
Reason (R): Under the Ryotwari settlement, the assessment was ordinarily revised about every thirty years.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
naf8ca318a1e.x: Both are features of Ryotwari, but periodic revision does not explain why revenue was fixed on land.

n6756b66cff4.s: In Coastal Andhra, zamindars of the Zamindari areas paid the Company:
n6756b66cff4.x: Coastal lands were divided into Haveli (direct Company control) and Zamindari areas, whose zamindars paid peshkash.

nindian-history-110-12.s: The Ryotwari system was first begun, from 1792, in:
nindian-history-110-12.x: Ryotwari began in Baramahal from 1792; its main area was Madras.

nee8ba3058ab.s: In the Andhra region, Thomas Munro first introduced Ryotwari in 1802 in:
nee8ba3058ab.x: Munro brought Ryotwari to the Ceded Districts (Rayalaseema) in 1802; the Northern Circars were mainly zamindari.

nindian-history-110-6.s: The Ryotwari Settlement is associated with Thomas Munro and:
nindian-history-110-6.x: Ryotwari is linked to Thomas Munro and Alexander Read; the Permanent Settlement to Cornwallis.

n646f5dbd57a.s: Absentee landlordism, sub-infeudation and rack-renting were effects of the:
n646f5dbd57a.x: These, along with peasants reduced to tenants-at-will, were effects of the Permanent Settlement.

n7a326e481b0.s: The three major British land-revenue settlements made land a:
n7a326e481b0.x: The settlements made land transferable, created a loyal landlord class and fed rural indebtedness and peasant revolts.

naf98b4bc771.s: Sir Thomas Munro, who died of cholera at Pattikonda in 1827, was buried at:
naf98b4bc771.x: Munro died at Pattikonda (Kurnool) in 1827 and was buried at Gooty; Anantapur was his headquarters as Collector.

n8349de27ab7.s: The Permanent Settlement initially began as a ____ settlement.
n8349de27ab7.x: It began as a ten-year (decennial) settlement and was later made permanent.

nb9ef4cfa59a.s: The Mahalwari System was proposed in 1822 by:
nb9ef4cfa59a.x: Holt Mackenzie proposed it in 1822; it was revised under Bentinck in 1833 with R.M. Bird.

nf4762aa6699.s: The Permanent Settlement was introduced in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa in:
nf4762aa6699.x: It was introduced in 1793 (not 1795), planned by Cornwallis with John Shore.

na330ec3dd14.s: Baramahal came under Company control after the Third Mysore War in:
na330ec3dd14.x: Baramahal came under the Company in 1792, before the Permanent Settlement was made permanent (1793).

nindian-history-110-5.s: Under the Mahalwari system, the revenue relationship was between the Government and the:
nindian-history-110-5.x: The Permanent Settlement dealt with the zamindar, Ryotwari with the ryot and Mahalwari with the village or mahal.

n68b6e8f7902.s: The Permanent Settlement was applied in the Circars and Ryotwari introduced in Rayalaseema in:
n68b6e8f7902.x: These settlements came in 1802, after Guntur (1788), Padmanabham (1794) and the Ceded Districts (1800).

nb7c5548457d.s: Early in his career, Thomas Munro served in the Baramahal as assistant to:
nb7c5548457d.x: Munro was Assistant to Read in the Baramahal, then Principal Collector of the Ceded Districts, President of the Judicial Commission and Governor of Madras.

nindian-history-110-15.s: Under the Ryotwari system, after a bad harvest:
o: an automatic general exemption from revenue was granted
occasional remission or reduction of revenue was possible
nindian-history-110-15.x: Ryotwari gave no automatic exemption, but occasional remission or reduction was possible.

nfdd06784d6c.s: Under the Mahalwari System, revenue was collected by the:
nfdd06784d6c.x: The lambardar collected under Mahalwari; the zamindar under the Permanent Settlement and the individual farmer under Ryotwari.

n93ae354794f.s: In the Madras Presidency, the Northern Circars were mainly under the:
n93ae354794f.x: The Northern Circars were mainly zamindari; Haveli lands under direct British control later came under Ryotwari.

nc8ac4488cb9.s: Under the Mahalwari System, default in revenue payment made:
o: the zamindar's estate liable to auction
nc8ac4488cb9.x: Under Mahalwari the village was collectively liable; under Ryotwari the cultivator's land could be seized.

nff7e48bebe1.s: Under the zamindari arrangement, the gains from agriculture went mainly to the:
nff7e48bebe1.x: Under the zamindari system, gains from agriculture went to the zamindars, not to the Company.

nb2fc444c5f1.s: Under the Ryotwari and Mahalwari systems, the revenue assessment was:
nb2fc444c5f1.x: Revenue was fixed forever under the Permanent Settlement, but periodically revised under Ryotwari and Mahalwari.

nfae1249ed64.s: The criticism that the State became the 'ultimate landlord' was directed at the:
nfae1249ed64.x: Critics held that under Ryotwari the state became the ultimate landlord and its revenue was as heavy as zamindari rent.

n13b822baa4e.s: John Shore helped Cornwallis plan the:
n13b822baa4e.x: John Shore helped plan the Permanent Settlement; Ryotwari was linked to Read and Munro and Mahalwari to Holt Mackenzie.

n5798d1eee41.s: The need to pay land revenue in cash encouraged the cultivation of:
o: commercial crops such as indigo, cotton, opium and jute
n5798d1eee41.x: Cash revenue demands pushed peasants to grow commercial crops such as indigo, cotton, opium and jute.

nee2cb4818c0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the stages of colonialism in India?
o: The mercantilist stage (1757-1813) saw Company trade monopoly and direct plunder.
In the free-trade stage (1813-1858) India became a market for British goods and a source of raw materials.
The Charter Act of 1813 opened the free-trade stage.
nee2cb4818c0.x: The finance-capital stage began in 1858; 1813 opened the free-trade stage.

n2e3ca83a520.s: Which of the following was NOT a cause of deindustrialisation in India?
o: Railways carrying British goods into the interior
British traders being denied special privileges
Transit and customs duties hurting indigenous trade
Artisans being forced to reveal trade secrets
n2e3ca83a520.x: British traders actually received special privileges, so that statement is false. (No dates for a sequence, so written as a NOT question from the original statements.)

ned9072624ed.s: The interest component of the drain of wealth was interest on public debt raised in:
ned9072624ed.x: The interest was on public debt raised in Britain, not on loans from Indian peasants. (No dates for a sequence, so written as a one-liner.)

ndd492febd42.s: The Famine Commission of 1880, whose report led to the Famine Code of 1883, was headed by:
ndd492febd42.x: Strachey's 1880 commission followed the 1876-78 famine and led to the 1883 Famine Code; Campbell was 1866, Lyall 1897-98, MacDonnell 1901.

nd9fb807519c.s: India's export surplus under colonial rule was mainly used to:
o: bring gold and silver into India
meet British office and war expenses
nd9fb807519c.x: The export surplus did not bring matching gold or silver; it financed British office and war expenses.

n04d383e4d4e.s: The Hilton Young Commission (1926) fixed the rupee at:
n04d383e4d4e.x: It fixed the rupee at 1s 6d; Indian business wanted 1s 4d. Its central bank proposal led to the RBI (1935).

nf1c08f873c8.s: India's first jute mill was set up in 1855 at:
nf1c08f873c8.x: The first jute mill was set up at Rishra in Bengal in 1855.

nb3a7b510012.s: The Guntur famine of 1832-33 is known as:
nb3a7b510012.x: The Guntur famine of 1832-33 is called Dokkala or Nandana Karuvu.

nb78e30cd9c8.s: Deindustrialisation in colonial India went along with an agriculture that remained:
nb78e30cd9c8.x: Indian industry declined through loss of markets while agriculture stayed stagnant with low productivity.

nf48381f64e0.s: The Dutch set up their first factory in Andhra at:
nf48381f64e0.x: The Dutch set up their first Andhra factory at Machilipatnam, famous for chintz, dyed fabrics and muslins.

nc207095a923.s: Dadabhai Naoroji first stated the drain argument in:
nc207095a923.x: Naoroji first stated the drain in 'England's Debt to India' (1867); 'Economic History of India' is R.C. Dutt's.

nceb0c805d86.s: The Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act (1879) followed the:
nceb0c805d86.x: The Act, protecting peasants against moneylenders, followed the Deccan riots of 1875.

na3bc0afea7d.s: Who said the British had 'inundated the very mother country of cotton with cottons'?

n8a659efebde.s: Ponduru, known for fine hand-spun khadi, is in ____ district.
n8a659efebde.x: Ponduru is associated with Srikakulam; Uppada is known for jamdani silk.

n44df11c95c6.s: On the eve of independence, foreign-owned jute mills were concentrated in:
n44df11c95c6.x: Indian-owned cotton mills were in Maharashtra and Gujarat, and foreign-owned jute mills in Bengal.

n20c00b36dd0.s: Which Act ended the Company's Indian trade monopoly and opened India to British machine-made goods?
n20c00b36dd0.x: The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's monopoly and opened India to British machine-made goods.

n23e1ee9c2ad.s: Of the eleven famines Andhra suffered in the late 19th century, the most severe was that of:
n23e1ee9c2ad.x: Andhra suffered eleven famines in the late 19th century, 1865-66 being the most severe.

nd5c25ee0a57.s: Who fed the people during the Kurnool famine of 1866 and later received a gold medal from Queen Victoria?
nd5c25ee0a57.x: Budda Vengalareddy of Uyyalawada fed the people and received the medal on 1 January 1877.

n77a3da08cad.s: In response to the drain of wealth, the Moderates demanded:
n77a3da08cad.x: The Moderates demanded cuts in military spending, lower land revenue, abolition of the salt tax and protective tariffs.

n8d401edfa1f.s: British investors in Indian railways were guaranteed a return of:
n8d401edfa1f.x: Railway investors were guaranteed 5% whether or not the lines earned.

n986c670963d.s: Under the Tinkathiya system, indigo had to be grown on ____ of each holding.
n986c670963d.x: Tinkathiya required indigo on 3/20 of each holding.

nd01c5e50dca.s: Famines became frequent in areas of commercialised agriculture mainly because:
o: cash crops replaced food crops, reducing food security
nd01c5e50dca.x: Replacement of food crops by cash crops cut food security and made famines more frequent.

n5cf285982b9.s: The higher rupee-sterling ratio (1s 6d) hurt Indian exporters because it:
o: made British imports dearer in India
n5cf285982b9.x: A higher ratio made Indian goods dearer abroad; it also made British imports cheaper, a separate effect.

n59bc7d36f70.s: On the eve of independence, agriculture employed over 75% of the workforce but contributed about ____ of GDP.
n59bc7d36f70.x: Agriculture employed over 75% of workers but gave only about 50% of GDP, showing low productivity.

n84f3a40053e.s: On the eve of independence, life expectancy in India was about:
n84f3a40053e.x: Per capita income was about Rs 265, life expectancy 32 years and literacy below 16%.

n0fcacf7ad0d.s: In the triangular trade between India, China and Britain, India sent to China:
n0fcacf7ad0d.x: Indian opium went to China, Chinese tea and silver to Britain, and British manufactures to India.

n36af816fed6.s: Under the Famine Code, gratuitous relief was meant for:
n36af816fed6.x: The Code gave relief works for the able-bodied and gratuitous relief for the old and infirm.

nf45db32374c.s: The nationalist critique rejected the view that colonial famines were caused exclusively by:
nf45db32374c.x: Rigid revenue collection and grain exports were key causes; famines were not due to monsoon failure alone.

ne8720ca321d.s: The last famine commission of the colonial period (1944) was the:
ne8720ca321d.x: The Woodhead Commission (1944) was the last; the Campbell Commission (1866) was the first.

n790a904265d.s: The Doji Bara famine occurred in:
n790a904265d.x: Doji Bara was in 1791-92, between the Great Bengal Famine (1770) and the Orissa-Ganjam famine (1865-66).

n04881b9e7ed.s: Arthur Cotton's Godavari anicut at Dowleswaram was sanctioned in:
n04881b9e7ed.x: It was reported in 1844, sanctioned in 1846, begun in 1847 and its main structure finished in April 1852.

n575b2458c61.s: The Great Famine of 1876-78, which affected Madras, Mysore, Hyderabad and Bombay, occurred under:
n575b2458c61.x: The Great Famine of 1876-78 occurred during Lytton's tenure.

nedad885b38f.s: The Krishna anicut at Bezwada was proposed by:
nedad885b38f.x: Colonel Henry Atlock Lake proposed the Krishna anicut at Bezwada.

n204260e7749.s: 'Open Letters to Lord Curzon' (1900) was written by:
n204260e7749.x: R.C. Dutt's Open Letters to Lord Curzon dates to 1900.

n2c127b263a4.s: During the Company period, famine policy was marked by:
o: no famine code and minimal relief
a comprehensive famine code and extensive relief
suspension of revenue in every famine
transfer of all relief to village councils
n2c127b263a4.x: The Company government never adopted a famine code and gave only minimal relief.

nap-history-19-28.s: Fergusson College (1885) was established by the:
nap-history-19-28.x: The Deccan Education Society, which promoted nationalist education, opened Fergusson College in 1885.

n49cd384c322.s: The London Missionary Society had its Andhra centre (1824) at:
n49cd384c322.x: The LMS centred on Kadapa (1824); Lutherans worked in Guntur, the North German Society in Rajahmundry-Eluru and the American Baptists in Ongole-Nellore.

n763c8c9d396.s: The Hunter Commission (1882) was appointed during the viceroyalty of:
n763c8c9d396.x: The Hunter Commission of 1882 came under Ripon; Curzon is linked with the 1902 Universities Commission.

nindian-history-14-32.x: Wood's Despatch came in 1854; the three universities in 1857 and the Hunter Commission in 1882.

naab44b04e82.s: Wood's Despatch (1854) was issued under Governor-General:
naab44b04e82.x: It was issued under Dalhousie, drafted by Wood as President of the Board of Control.

nff9cc268902.s: The English Education Act of 1835 was passed under:
nff9cc268902.x: The 1835 Act was passed under Bentinck on the basis of Macaulay's Minute.

nindian-history-108-16.s: Who chaired the Calcutta University Commission of 1917?
nindian-history-108-16.x: M.E. Sadler chaired it; Ashutosh Mukherjee was a member.

o: wastage and stagnation in primary education
nindian-history-124-9.x: Hartog reported on wastage and stagnation in primary education; Sadler on Calcutta University and Lee on the civil services.

n48c4609cdf1.s: The Resolution on Education Policy, 1913, answering Gokhale's demand for compulsory primary education, was issued under:
n48c4609cdf1.x: The 1913 Resolution came under Hardinge II; the Universities Act 1904 was Curzon's.

nec36f97882a.s: Wood's Despatch prescribed English for higher education and ____ for lower education.
nec36f97882a.x: Wood's Despatch used English at higher levels and vernacular languages at lower levels.

nindian-history-124-3.s: The Campbell Commission belongs to the era of:
nindian-history-124-3.x: The Campbell Commission belongs to the Sir John Lawrence era.

nd82604580c0.s: The Anglo-Vernacular School at Narsapur, with branches at Palakollu, Penugonda and Achanta, was established in:
nd82604580c0.x: The Narsapur Anglo-Vernacular School was set up in 1852 with branches at Palakollu, Penugonda and Achanta.

n69e6a7f6eba.s: The Sargent Plan (1944), proposing free compulsory education for ages 6-14, came during the viceroyalty of:
n69e6a7f6eba.x: The Sargent Plan came under Wavell; Irwin was Viceroy at the time of the Hartog Committee (1929).

nf3279e5328b.s: The General Committee of Public Instruction, which managed the education grant, was set up in:
nf3279e5328b.x: The GCPI was set up in 1823, ten years after the Charter Act of 1813, and split into Orientalist and Anglicist camps.

nindian-history-124-15.s: The Whitley Commission was appointed in:
nindian-history-124-15.x: The Whitley Commission was in 1929; the Simon Commission and Butler Committee in 1927 and the Lee Commission in 1924.

n536fa8e7ecd.s: The Rs 1 lakh a year earmarked by the Charter Act of 1813 was actually released only in the:
n536fa8e7ecd.x: The Act earmarked Rs 1 lakh a year for literature and science, but the money was released only in the 1830s.

nindian-history-108-13.s: The Hunter Commission on education was appointed in:
nindian-history-108-13.x: The Hunter Commission was in 1882; Macaulay's Minute 1835, Wood's Despatch 1854, Hartog Committee 1929.

nindian-history-14-36.s: Curzon's University Commission (1902) was headed by:
nindian-history-14-36.x: It was headed by Sir Thomas Raleigh; Bilgrami and Gurudas Banerjee were its Indian members.

nindian-history-124-19.x: The Butler Committee dealt with princely states and paramountcy; Lee with the civil services and Whitley with labour.

nindian-history-14-22.s: Delhi College (1824) grew out of the Madrasa of:
nindian-history-14-22.x: Delhi College grew out of the Madrasa of Ghazi-ud-din Khan and predated Mayo College and MAO College (1875).

nindian-history-14-28.s: The Central Hindu School at Banaras (1898), later the nucleus of BHU, was set up by:
nindian-history-14-28.x: Annie Besant set up the Central Hindu School on 7 July 1898; it became the nucleus of BHU.

nindian-history-14-8.s: Wood's Despatch modelled the 1857 universities of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras on the University of:
nindian-history-14-8.x: They followed the University of London, then only an examining body, so they were affiliating and examining universities.

n6defbd8a149.s: The Government college at Rajahmundry was converted into a degree college in:
n6defbd8a149.x: Elphinstone's scheme (1839), regional school (1854), second-grade college (1873), degree college (1877).

nc7b161742e8.s: The Calcutta Madrasa was founded in:
nc7b161742e8.x: Calcutta Madrasa 1781, Asiatic Society 1784, Sanskrit College Benaras 1791, Fort William College 1800.

nap-history-19-3.s: Andhra University, first started at Bezawada, was shifted to Waltair in:
nap-history-19-3.x: Constituted under the 1925 Act, it opened at Bezawada in 1926 and moved to Waltair in 1930.

ne97da6a1651.s: The English Education Act was passed in:
ne97da6a1651.x: Charter Act 1813, GCPI 1823, English Education Act 1835 and Wood's Despatch 1854.

n11037716b3e.s:
Assertion (A): The Indian Press Act, 1910 revived features of the Vernacular Press Act with heavy security deposits.
Reason (R): The Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act, 1908 let magistrates seize the presses of papers inciting violence.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n11037716b3e.x: Both are true press laws of the Minto II era, but the 1908 Act's seizure power does not explain the 1910 Act's revival of VPA features.

n0124525efc9.s: Under the Vernacular Press Act, 1878, a paper could obtain exemption by:
o: submitting proofs to a government censor before publication
paying a fine to the magistrate
n0124525efc9.x: Exemption came by submitting proofs to a censor; magistrates could demand bonds and there was no appeal to a court. (No dates for a sequence, so written as a one-liner.)

n4d74e9b1a43.s: Amrita Bazar Patrika was founded by:
o: G. Subramania Iyer and M. Veeraraghavachariar
Sisir Kumar Ghosh and Motilal Ghosh
n4d74e9b1a43.x: Amrita Bazar Patrika was founded by the Ghosh brothers; The Hindu by Subramania Iyer and others; Kesari by Tilak.

nc6d1942726b.s: The first railway line in Andhra (1862) was:
nc6d1942726b.x: Puttur-Renigunta (1862) was Andhra's first line; South India's first ran Royapuram-Wallajah Road in 1856.

nd6fa6c556b7.s: Under the railway guarantee system, the 5% return to British companies was paid:
o: from Indian revenues whether or not the lines made a profit
only when the lines made a profit
nd6fa6c556b7.x: The guarantee was paid from Indian revenues regardless of profit, and nationalists counted it in the drain.

n7c239e93e01.s: The General Committee of Public Instruction (1823) was set up mainly to:
n7c239e93e01.x: The GCPI managed education funds; it was not a teacher-training body.

nd2044d90d2e.s: The Licensing Regulations of 1823, which penalised printing without a licence, were issued by acting Governor-General:
nd2044d90d2e.x: Acting G-G John Adams issued them; Metcalfe repealed them in 1835 and became 'liberator of the Indian press'.

n24165f52a3e.s: Which is called the 'Magna Carta of English Education in India'?
n24165f52a3e.x: Wood's Despatch (1854) is the Magna Carta; universities followed in 1857.

ne571b002dfb.s: An unintended effect of railways in colonial India was:
o: the creation of a national market
ne571b002dfb.x: Railways served colonial exploitation but unintentionally created a national market and sped nationalist mobilisation.

n4c10f025162.x: Mirat-ul-Akhbar was in Persian; Tahzeeb-ul-Akhlaq was in Urdu and Sambad Kaumudi in Bengali.

n49de7134296.s: Udant Martand of Jugal Kishore Shukla was the first ____ newspaper.
n49de7134296.x: Udant Martand was the first Hindi newspaper.

n2268f7ad2f9.s: Macaulay wrote his Minute (1835) as Law Member and President of the:
n2268f7ad2f9.x: Macaulay led the Anglicists and wrote the Minute as Law Member and GCPI President; Bentinck approved it.

nd076dc4098e.s: Wood's Despatch rejected the ____ approach to education.
nd076dc4098e.x: Wood's Despatch recommended grants-in-aid and mass instruction and rejected downward filtration.

nd84cbd51fc9.s: Macaulay's Minute (1835) recommended that education funds be spent only on:
o: English-medium teaching of Western science and literature
nd84cbd51fc9.x: The Minute wanted funds spent only on English-medium Western science and literature.

n20b7d871a39.s: The statutory basis of the Press Council is the Press Council Act of:
n20b7d871a39.x: The Press Council rests on the Press Council Act, 1978, and still lacks punitive powers.

n7dd0349a9bb.s: The Post Office Act of 1854, which introduced uniform postage and stamps, is associated with:
n7dd0349a9bb.x: The 1854 Post Office Act is associated with Dalhousie.

n97d4d869e41.s: Desamata, which supported the Home Rule movement, was the paper of:
n97d4d869e41.x: Desamata of Chilakamarti supported Home Rule with Andhra Patrika and Krishna Patrika.

n9fb397c6b05.s: The Press and Registration of Periodicals Act, 2023 replaced the Press and Registration of Books Act of:
n9fb397c6b05.x: The 2023 Act replaced the 1867 Act; the RNI is now the Press Registrar General of India.

n7b1ee8015b6.s: The Registration Act of 1867, dealing with printers and presses, is associated with:
n7b1ee8015b6.x: The 1867 Act on registration of printers and presses came under John Lawrence.

nc2386f87a0d.s: India's first telegraph line (1851), under W.B. O'Shaughnessy, ran from Calcutta to:
nc2386f87a0d.x: The first line ran Calcutta-Diamond Harbour in 1851.

n16be836e2b9.s: After the Vernacular Press Act was repealed in 1882, the pre-censorship clause was dropped and ____ was appointed.
n16be836e2b9.x: Ripon's repeal dropped pre-censorship and a press commissioner was appointed.

n7d3b3c7da47.s: Which paper turned itself into an English paper overnight to escape the Vernacular Press Act?
n7d3b3c7da47.x: Amrita Bazar Patrika became English overnight; The Hindu was already in English.

nindian-history-135-13.s: An official reason for railway development in colonial India was:
nindian-history-135-13.x: Faster movement, communication and troop movement were official reasons; the aim was British goods into Indian markets, not markets for Indian goods.

nindian-history-8-8.s: Hindoo Patriot was started in 1853 by:
nindian-history-8-8.x: Girish Chandra Ghosh started Hindoo Patriot in 1853; Harish Chandra Mukherjee later edited it.

nindian-history-109-16.s: Qaumi Awaz, the Urdu daily linked with Nehru and Rafi Ahmed Kidwai, was started at Lucknow in:
nindian-history-109-16.x: Qaumi Awaz was started at Lucknow in 1945.

nindian-history-135-19.s: The colonial economic purpose of railways was to carry raw materials to the ports and:
nindian-history-135-19.x: Railways carried raw materials to ports for export and British goods into Indian markets.

n0fee0abef98.s: The Indian press enjoyed relative freedom after the 1835 measure of:
n0fee0abef98.x: Metcalfe's 1835 measure freed the press; Lytton's 1878 Act gagged it until Ripon's 1882 repeal.

n6e25d47c4b1.s: Telugu journalism is traced to the year:
n6e25d47c4b1.x: Telugu journalism dates from 1835, with Machilipatnam and Rajahmundry as early centres.

nff1c3c8c988.s: Which journal was associated with Kandukuri Veeresalingam?
nff1c3c8c988.x: Veeresalingam ran Vivekavardhini, Hasyasanjivani and Sati Hitabodhini; Andhra Kesari was Gadicherla's.

nce058eed195.s: In the education debate, the Orientalists favoured:
o: classical Sanskrit, Arabic and Persian learning
nce058eed195.x: Orientalists backed Sanskrit, Arabic and Persian learning; Anglicists backed Western science and English.

n03c418a3415.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about local self-government in colonial India?
o: Village panchayats were set up in several provinces after the Government of India Act, 1919.
Non-officials entered panchayats, municipal councils and district boards after 1882.
Local bodies were often starved of funds.
Local bodies after Ripon's Resolution were entirely free from official control.
n03c418a3415.x: Local bodies remained controlled by colonial officials and short of funds.

nad2b33355b8.s: Which is regarded as the 'Magna Carta of local self-government'?
nad2b33355b8.x: Ripon's Resolution is the Magna Carta; Mayo's dealt with financial decentralisation.

n6cc56a16915.s: The Lee Commission (1923-24), which proposed 50:50 parity in the ICS, was appointed under:
n6cc56a16915.x: The Lee Commission came under Reading; Hardinge II was Viceroy for the Islington Commission.

n53826829725.s: The Indian Civil Service is the direct ancestor of the:
n53826829725.x: The ICS is the direct ancestor of the IAS.

n6bf56a3abbf.s: The Aitchison Commission (1886) classified the services as:
n6bf56a3abbf.x: Aitchison (1886, Dufferin) replaced covenanted/uncovenanted with Imperial, Provincial and Subordinate.

nf6aa26aca1c.s: The Macaulay Committee recommended that the civil service examination be held in:
nf6aa26aca1c.x: It recommended the examination in London and preference for Oxford and Cambridge graduates.

nb30fe69ba7f.s: Munro's Judicial Commission recommended placing police supervision under the:
nb30fe69ba7f.x: Munro recommended police under the Collector and minor crimes tried by village officers.

nb32f60764af.s: Which body supported the Ilbert Bill against European agitation?
nb32f60764af.x: The Indian Association supported the Bill; the controversy exposed British racial attitudes.

n82326b3d245.s: The Police Act of 1861, passed under Canning, modelled the force on the:
n82326b3d245.x: The 1861 police was modelled on the Royal Irish Constabulary and meant to suppress dissent.

n4e2b01f7b0e.s: Under Cornwallis, provincial courts of appeal were set up at Calcutta, Dacca, Murshidabad and:
n4e2b01f7b0e.x: The four provincial courts of appeal were at Calcutta, Dacca, Murshidabad and Patna.

n7aecd060d7d.s: The first step towards financial decentralisation was Lord Mayo's Resolution of:
n7aecd060d7d.x: Mayo's 1870 Resolution began financial decentralisation and divided central and provincial finances.

nindian-history-134-15.s: The Allahabad High Court was set up in:
nindian-history-134-15.x: Calcutta, Bombay and Madras High Courts were the first set (1862); Allahabad came in 1866.

ndf12504a1a5.s: Lord Ripon's Resolution on local self-government was issued in:
ndf12504a1a5.x: Mayo 1870, Ripon 1882, GoI Act 1919 and GoI Act 1935.

nindian-history-134-12.s: The High Courts replaced the Supreme Courts and the Sadar Adalats under the:
nindian-history-134-12.x: The Indian High Courts Act of 1861 abolished the Supreme Courts and Sadar Adalats and set up High Courts.

nindian-history-134-13.s: The High Courts in India were established through:
o: Letters Patent issued under Crown authority
a resolution of the Board of Control
nindian-history-134-13.x: The High Courts were set up by Letters Patent issued under the Crown's authority.

nd674667e8b6.s: Under Cornwallis's civil service reforms, promotion was based largely on:
nd674667e8b6.x: Cornwallis created a covenanted service, banned private trade and gifts, and based promotion on seniority.

n192ff360118.s: Under Lytton's Statutory Civil Service (1878-79), the share of covenanted posts set aside for Indians of high families was:
n192ff360118.x: Lytton reserved one-sixth of covenanted posts for Indians of high families; the scheme was later abolished.
